topics.flagship-ru-ua: Bloomberg reportedly presented data from opposition hacker groups who breached Rosstat, indicating nearly 400,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine, concentrated in Russia's poorest regions, and raising the possibility of a new mobilisation; this is unverified and carried by two outlets. A fourth round of Russia-US-Ukraine talks in 2026 is set for Abu Dhabi this week, with security guarantees high on the agenda and a 'no concession' Russian posture expected. On the eve of the talks, Russia hit Ukraine's power grid and Ukraine targeted a major Russian oil refinery, while a Russian winter strike campaign is causing blackouts and heating loss. Police have identified 30 of 55 bodies from the Komyshuvakha strike, with up to 19 more possibly under rubble. Novaya Gazeta closed its Moscow offices citing government pressure, and Europe remains split over leader-level calls to Putin.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Torrential rain collapsed a sand embankment onto tents in Gaza, killing a woman and three small children, and highlighting flood risk for hundreds of thousands of displaced Palestinians while Israel continues to block mobile homes. Houthi rebels say at least 44 people, most of them women, were killed in airstrikes near Yemen's capital. Secretary of State Rubio defended the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began February 28, as 'necessary' to prevent a nuclear weapon even while linking it to Republican midterm losses. Other reporting covers at least 25 seafarer deaths per the IMO, Iran's use of Hormuz attacks as leverage, and a reported domestic security crackdown in Iran amid US strike threats.
topics.T15: The BBC says it has a 'Black Sky' plan to keep the UK informed over emergency FM radio during prolonged blackouts, with a self-sufficient studio ready for 72 hours. Separate coverage of the European Commission's call for 72-hour household supplies reports public concern and rising retail demand for survival gear. Other items cover a WMO warning that a strong El Niño could intensify heat and rainfall extremes through 2027, COP31 climate-vulnerability coverage, and hurricane-preparedness pieces, some of which look dated.
topics.T01: Coverage is sparse and single-sourced. The UKPNP alleges Pakistani forces used drones, mortars and heavy weapons on civilian areas in Rawalakot in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, causing deaths. Other items are commentary on Black Sea militarization and Turkish strait policy, and a Cuban UN envoy's warning of a potential US conflict via Russian media.
topics.T02: Coverage is a scattering of single-source items. The UN reports one in three Afghans facing severe hunger as winter approaches, with over 4 million children under five needing malnutrition treatment in 2027. A UN agency says El Niño could cost the global economy up to $11 trillion and threaten food security. Other items cover a Sudan teachers' strike over pay, 3.68 million displaced Nigerians, Manipur relief-camp mental health problems, and ASEAN's Myanmar aid mission.
topics.T03: Israeli intelligence has reportedly warned the US that Iran may be considering chemical weapons use against adversaries if regional tensions escalate, according to a New York Times report relayed by a single secondary outlet. The report says the warning has divided US officials. No corroboration is provided in the input.
topics.T04: Stories are sparse and generic. A British Veterinary Association survey finds fewer than a third of UK vets think the profession is prepared for a major animal disease outbreak, and a Texas county medical reserve corps is recruiting volunteers. A zero-source headline snippet cites CDC reports of more than 5,000 US measles cases, but it is unverified here.
topics.T05: Only one story: President Trump signed an order on November 3 renewing the national emergency declared over Nicaragua, citing an 'unusual and extraordinary threat' that dates from November 2018. This is a routine annual renewal rather than a new development.
topics.T06: Reuters, citing an internal EU assessment, reports that a covert Russian network used social media to exploit last month's French riots, blaming unrest on immigration and portraying the government as having lost control. A 60 Minutes segment cited by one outlet says the unrest has damaged 2,500 businesses, injured over 1,500 police and caused more than $1 billion in damage, including the arson of Limoges town hall on Oct. 17. It also describes Marine Le Pen as the favorite for April's presidential election. A separate item discusses statutory history of the Insurrection Act and the Newsom v. Trump ruling.
topics.T08: A gunman reportedly fascinated by the far right killed six and wounded at least 15 in Krakow's historic center on Nov. 7, in Poland's deadliest shooting in decades. Reports from a single outlet say militants killed more than 50 people in Daleti, western Ethiopia, and that a policeman was killed and three are missing after an attack on a checkpost in Hangu, Pakistan. Other coverage notes high arrest numbers under the UK's Palestine Action proscription.
topics.T10: Congress returns with funding, Pete Hegseth and the debt limit on the agenda, with Republicans holding majorities for under two months. Reporting says Trump's battleship and Golden Dome plans are in doubt after the midterms, and defense contractors may face more scrutiny in a new Congress. North Korea reportedly tested a new high-speed torpedo and plans to deploy the AI-equipped weapon by early 2027. Other items include US Army relay drones borrowing from Ukrainian practice, China's reported record $583 billion research budget, and Canada's increased military spending.
topics.T11: India's INS Surat reached Muscat for a naval exercise with Oman. Analysis says a European military exercise highlights Europe's bid for a role in Ukraine peace talks. The UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force will reportedly expand its naval posture in the North Atlantic and Arctic, and 7,000 US troops are exercising across Hawaii through Nov. 17.
topics.T12: Cyberattacks on refrigeration systems have hit European retailers again, and US federal agencies warned on Nov. 5 that hackers are targeting industrial freezers and cold storage that hold food and medicine. Analysts say there is no broader market contagion from a reported $6.3 billion Binance hack, since the exchange pledged to cover losses. Other items include Indonesia urging banks to bolster cyber defenses and a weekly vulnerability recap; one analysis asks whether recent events signal a hacking epidemic.
topics.T13: At least 34 people died when a Europe-bound migrant boat sank off Senegal, on the Atlantic route to Spain's Canary Islands. A Spanish tourist territory has reportedly declared an emergency after a surge in small-boat arrivals, fearing it is 'the new Ceuta'. Both are single-source reports.
topics.T14: The US reportedly declared Lebanese consul in Detroit Ibrahim Charara persona non grata and gave him 48 hours to leave, over old social media posts praising the 1983 Beirut Marine barracks bombing. The account comes from a single outlet, relaying Asharq Al-Awsat and Lebanese Foreign Ministry sources, and follows a Washington Free Beacon report.
topics.T16: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' net worth, after tech leaders spent hundreds of millions against it. Congress returns for a lame-duck session after Democratic midterm gains. One outlet says Trump questioned the midterm results and revived voting-machine claims, while in a 60 Minutes interview he appeared to accept defeat. Other items: South Africa's local elections marked a decline in ANC dominance, New Zealand's close election has delayed coalition talks, and France's protests may boost Le Pen.

bluf: A woman and three small children were killed in Gaza when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in torrential rain, underscoring the flood risk to displaced Palestinians as winter sets in. Houthi rebels say at least 44 people, most of them women, were killed in airstrikes near Yemen's capital, and the attribution of the strikes is not given in the input. Bloomberg reportedly presented hacked Rosstat data from opposition groups indicating nearly 400,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine and raising the possibility of a new mobilisation; the data is unverified. A fourth round of Russia-US-Ukraine talks is set for Abu Dhabi this week, with security guarantees high on the agenda and a 'no concession' Russian stance expected. The day before, Russia and Ukraine traded long-range strikes, with Russia hitting Ukraine's power grid and Ukraine targeting a major Russian oil refinery. An internal EU assessment seen by Reuters says a covert Russian network exploited last month's French riots on social media to blame immigration and portray the government as having lost control. Separately, Israeli intelligence has reportedly warned the US that Iran may be considering chemical weapons use, according to a single-source relay of a New York Times report. A gunman reportedly fascinated by the far right also killed six in Krakow on Nov. 7, in Poland's deadliest shooting in decades.
